taglines: It is Thursday. Friday is visible from here but do not be deceived. Thursday is its own sovereign nation with its own laws and its own unsettling amount of remaining work. Do not let Friday's proximity fool you into coasting. Thursday will notice.

Someone on your team just said 'we should sync on this' and you both know it means the thing is not getting done this week. The sync is the polite way of admitting it. The sync is a eulogy for the deadline.

You have seventeen browser tabs open. One of them is the actual thing you need. The other sixteen are the journey you took trying to find it. You will not close them. You will never close them. They are load-bearing now.

The coffee you made yourself is objectively worse than coffee shop coffee. You have tried everything. Different beans. Different ratios. A grinder that cost $140. The problem is not the beans. The problem is that you made it yourself at home and the context ruins it.
An AI helped you do something in four minutes that used to take an hour. You did not use the remaining 56 minutes well. You used them to find something else to worry about. You have a gift.

It is 9am on a Thursday and someone has already sent a message that starts with 'Quick question —'. There is no such thing as a quick question. A quick question is a question that has not yet revealed its full size. The quick question always blooms.

Thursday exists to remind you that you had goals for this week. Some of them were reasonable. A few of them were optimistic. One of them was genuinely delusional and you knew it Monday morning but wrote it down anyway because ambition is embarrassing and beautiful and you cannot help yourself.

The most productive thing you will do today is the thing you kept putting off until the urgency made it unavoidable. Urgency is a terrible project manager but it gets results. Terrible, last-minute, somehow-fine results.
